title: I Forwarded the Wedding Plus-One Ban to the Cousin Who Brought Three

parts.text: I stood at the seating chart at 5:40 p.m. with a marker that was already running because my cousin Marla had written three extra names in gel pen. The invite said no plus-ones unless named. I was twenty-eight, maid of honor, holding place cards that smelled like cardstock and panic. Marla said family doesn't count as plus-ones. Her three extras were coworkers. The bride was in the suite crying about chicken counts. I photographed the invite, the gel pen, and the meal list. Then Marla posted in the family chat: they tried to turn me away like a stranger. The strangers were already eating the passed appetizers.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She posted that we turned her away while her coworkers ate the appetizers.

social.video_title: She gel-penned three extras onto the seating chart — Part 1/2
social.description: Place cards, chicken counts, and coworkers who were suddenly family. Would you have pulled the extra chairs?

parts.text: I dropped the invite photo into the same chat and the catering minimum. Marla's coworkers offered to leave. I let two leave and one stay because one chicken existed. Marla called me bridezilla adjacent. I was adjacent to a spreadsheet. The dance went on. The gel pen smeared. The bride ate a roll and stopped crying. I kept the seating chart as a PDF. Family counted. Coworkers counted as RSVPs. The appetizers ran out at a normal time instead of an emergency time.

social.video_title: The chat got the invite photo and the chicken math — Part 2/2
social.description: Two extras left, one chicken stayed, gel pen lost. Was a coworker a plus-one?
